div.head: AN EXPOSITION WITH NOTES On the EPISTLE of JUDE.

epigraph.q: Jude the Servant of Jeſus Chriſt, and Brother of James, to them that are ſanctified by God the Father, preſerved in Jeſus Chriſt, and called.

div.p: THis Epiſtle, as others, beginneth with uſual Chriſtian ſalutations; theſe are continued through the two firſt Verſes, in which you have,

epigraph.q: And of ſome have compaſſion, making a difference.
And others ſave with fear, pulling them out of the fire, hating even the garment ſpotted by the fleſh.

div.p: HEre is the ſecond part of the Exhortation, explaining their duty towards others, or teaching them how to behave themſelves to them that were gone aſtray.

epigraph.q: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to preſent you faultleſs before the preſence of his glory, with exceeding joy.

div.p: THe Apoſtle having perſwaded them to duty, now commendeth them to the divine grace, as 'tis uſual with the Apoſtles to ſhut up their Exhortations with prayer, to intimate that the fruit of all muſt be expected from God, without whoſe bleſſing Exhortations or Endeavours would be nothing.

epigraph.q: To the only wiſe God, our Saviour, be glory and majeſty, dominion and power, now and ever, Amen.

div.p: THe Apoſtle in this verſe goeth on with that doxology which he had begun in the former, here you may take notice of the deſcription of the perſon to whom the praiſe is given, he is diſcribed 1. By his excellency, the only wiſe God. 2. By our intereſt and the benefit we receive by him, and our Saviour.

epigraph.q: Bleſſed be his glorious Name for ever, and let the whole earth be filled with his glory: Amen, and Amen,
